evidence.title: Replace the accumulate loop in TagNormaliser with a collection pipeline
evidence.why: The loop builds $seen by hand and rescans it with in_array for each tag. uniqueStrict() keeps the strict comparison the test relies on ('0', '00' and '1e3' stay distinct), and array_values keeps the list<string> return type without a temp variable or @var. The trim callback is written out because map() passes the key as a second argument, which trim(...) would take as its character list.

evidence.title: Remove or wire up AllowedHosts and ProductCodes: nothing uses them
evidence.why: AllowedHosts is bound as a singleton and read from config/hosts.php, but no controller, middleware or route resolves it; ProductCodes is not referenced at all. Both exist only for their own unit tests. Confirm nothing outside this repository depends on them before deleting.

evidence.title: Use #[Fillable] without accepted on Offer, and cast accepted and price_cents
evidence.why: accepted is a state the server decides, so it should not be mass-assignable (factories write unguarded, so tests are unaffected). Without a cast, accepted comes back from the database as 0/1. User already uses attributes, so Offer and Order follow the same house style. The scopeAccepted name is kept on purpose: 'accepted' is a column, and a #[Scope] method of that name would break $offer->accepted wherever the column is not loaded.

evidence.title: Delete the TrimStrings stub that repeats the framework defaults
evidence.why: Nothing registers App\Http\Middleware\TrimStrings, and its $except list is identical to the parent's (current_password, password, password_confirmation), so it is dead code either way.
evidence.suggested: // delete app/Http/Middleware/TrimStrings.php

evidence.title: Aggregate revenue in SQL instead of hydrating every order
evidence.why: The report loads every order as a model and sums in PHP, so memory and time grow with the orders table on a public endpoint. A grouped sum returns one row per country.
evidence.suggested:
return Order::query()
            ->selectRaw('country, sum(total_cents) as revenue')
            ->groupBy('country')
            ->orderBy('country')
            ->pluck('revenue', 'country')
            ->map(fn (mixed $revenue): int => (int) $revenue)
            ->all();

evidence.title: Validate offer input in a FormRequest and stop mass-assigning raw input
evidence.why: create() receives $request->all(), and 'accepted' is fillable but never validated, so any caller can post accepted=true and create an offer that is already accepted (probed: POST with accepted=true returned accepted: true). Inline validate() is also the only place the rules live.

evidence.title: Replace the accumulate loop in TagNormaliser with a collection pipeline
evidence.why: This is an accumulate-in-foreach with a strict `in_array`. The pipeline keeps strict comparison via `uniqueStrict()`, so `'0'` and `'00'` stay distinct, which the existing test pins. `->all()` is not typed as a list, hence the `array_values()` wrapper and no temp variable. Use the closure for `trim`: `map(trim(...))` would pass the collection key as trim's second argument.

evidence.title: Remove unused AllowedHosts, ProductCodes and the stock TrimStrings copy
evidence.why: `grep -rn` over `app routes config bootstrap` finds `AllowedHosts` only in the provider that binds it and `ProductCodes` nowhere; only their own unit tests use them. The app `TrimStrings` is not registered in `bootstrap/app.php`, and it repeats the parent's `$except` list (`current_password`, `password`, `password_confirmation`) exactly, so it changes nothing either way. Confirm nothing outside this repo depends on them before deleting.

evidence.title: Validate offer creation in a FormRequest and stop writing request->all()
evidence.why: `Offer::create([...$request->all()])` hands every posted key to a model whose `$fillable` includes `accepted`. In a scratch run a guest POST with `accepted: true` created an accepted offer, and `accepted: null` returned a 500 (NOT NULL violation). The `price_cents` rule also has no upper bound, and the column is `unsignedInteger`, so a larger value passes validation and fails at the database on MySQL. A FormRequest with `validated()` closes all three. The 50-item and 50-character tag caps and the 4294967295 price cap are suggested limits; adjust them to the product.

evidence.title: Stop reporting accepted=false for offers whose flag was never loaded
evidence.why: `GET /api/offers/titles` selects only `id` and `title`, so `$this->accepted` is unset and the resource answers `accepted: false` for every row, including accepted offers. The existing test hides it: it asserts `false` on row 0, which happens to be the one non-accepted offer. In a scratch run an accepted offer came back as `{"id":1,"title":"A","accepted":false}`. `whenHas` omits the key when the column was not selected. The model default (`$attributes`) and the `boolean` cast keep `accepted: false` in the create response and make index return real booleans. If clients need the flag in the titles list, add `accepted` to that `select()` instead.

evidence.title: Use #[Fillable] like User and keep accepted out of the mass-assignable list
evidence.why: `User` already uses the Laravel 13 `#[Fillable]` attribute while `Offer` and `Order` still use the property. `accepted` is a state flag that no request should set, so it leaves the fillable list (factories bypass guarding, so tests still create accepted offers). `scopeAccepted()` is deliberately not converted to `#[Scope]`: `accepted` is also a column, and a scope method with the same name would break `$offer->accepted` on the partial select used by `titles`.

Casting to an object keeps the non-empty output byte-identical and makes the empty case `{}`.

evidence.title: Validate offer list filters and paginate the list
evidence.why: `?accepted=banana` is silently treated as 'no filter', and the list is unbounded: every offer is loaded and serialised on each request. The rewrite adds a FormRequest and `paginate()`. Two edge cases came up in a scratch run: `?accepted=true` must stay valid, so the rule is `in:0,1,true,false` (the built-in `boolean` rule would reject it), and a blank `?per_page=` arrives as `null`, so the controller uses `integer('per_page') ?: 25`. The list response now carries `links` and `meta` next to `data`. `titles()` is unbounded too; paginate it the same way if the table grows.
